absent: Exact power-group name string and energy-bias register encoding
Hotplug state numeric values and suspend-resume sequence details
Model-specific normal hint values beyond the powersave marker
Scalable bank family enum values and architectural maximum bank count
Machine-check register field semantics beyond mask positions
Firmware record identifier allocation and persistence guarantees
Decoder chain priority numeric bounds and notifier handling
LVT offset programming and interrupt routing details
Threshold restart programming sequence on the target CPU
Legacy memory-error test criteria when scalable mode is off

findings.text: Block fan-out per machine-check bank is five. The largest programmable threshold value is 4095. Threshold APIC signalling uses selector value 131072.

High-word decoding uses top-bit valid, next-bit counter-present and next-bit locked. Offset, enable, type-pair, overflow and twelve-bit count occupy progressively lower fields. Low-word linkage uses its top byte. Masks equal 2147483648 and 1073741824 and 536870912 and 15728640 and 524288 and 393216 and 65536 and 4095 and 4278190080 in definition order, with window base 3221226496.
Combined-unit default error register lives at extended address 3221226512. Its LVT offset subfield selects among sixteen values using mask 240. Scalable threshold LVT disable uses offset value 61440.
Generated machine-check type names are bounded to thirty bytes including termination. Spin delay unit is one hundred nanoseconds. Bank attribute names are bounded to sixteen bytes.
Error-record interchange uses two fixed firmware identifiers, one marking the creator as machine-check and one marking the section type as machine-check, both stable across boots.

Per-CPU machine-check state keeps two bank collections for threshold and deferred delivery plus single-bit enables for each path. One global flag records whether threshold interrupt mode is active. Legacy banks are labelled by position with six functional names. Scalable UMC blocks use two fixed labels for memory and miscellaneous paths.

Hardware identity pairs a small integer bank family with a combined hardware and type code. Per-bank runtime state links to that identity, records instance and user-visible numbering, and carries a single physical-address-valid flag with reserved space. Instances are held per CPU across the maximum bank count.

User-visible scalable-bank names form a dense table indexed by bank family, with versioned families sharing labels except memory controllers which keep distinct version labels. Lookup returns no name when the family is out of range. A separate constant table binds each family to its hardware and type pair, including a zero pair for reserved.

Threshold configuration is organised as banks containing blocks. Each block records its position, parent bank, owning CPU, register address, interrupt capability and current limit, plus sysfs linkage and list membership. Each bank holds a sysfs anchor and a list head. Per-CPU state holds the bank pointer array and a bitmask of owned banks. One shared character scratch area bounded by the name limit supports generated names.

Deferred-error delivery enters through a dedicated system vector whose handling combines entry-exit tracing with statistics, dispatch through a mutable function pointer and completion signalling. The initial pointer reports unexpected delivery. Two installed helpers poll respectively the deferred and threshold bank collections on the local CPU with timestamping.
Restart context bundles a target block pointer with LVT offset control and the previous limit, allowing a remote CPU to reprogram one threshold from sysfs context.
Legacy fourth-bank naming distinguishes addresses 1043 and 3221226504 and 3221226505 as memory, interconnect and cache roles, warning and yielding an empty label otherwise.

Memory-error classification checks that low extended status bits are clear and that the bank family on the reporting CPU is a memory-controller variant. Dispatch selects the scalable test when that mode is active and the legacy test otherwise.

Threshold sysfs attributes share a common descriptor carrying name, access mode and show plus store callbacks specialised to blocks. Limit and count are always present, with count read-only and limit read-write, while interrupt-enable appears only when the block advertises capability. A small fixed attribute vector holds these entries with termination.

Reprogramming is performed on the owning CPU with the prior limit retained for restart. Accepted numeric inputs are clamped into one through the ceiling, with non-numeric rejected and unreachable owner reported as missing. Count display derives from the live register minus programmed headroom, likewise reporting missing when the owner is offline.

Sysfs dispatch recovers block and attribute containers from generic kernel objects and delegates to the attribute-specific callbacks, signalling I/O error when a callback is absent. Operations and object type bind these dispatchers with default groups and a release handler.

Threshold sysfs lifecycle moves from absent to populated to torn down. Population is skipped unless the feature is active and no instance exists, proceeds only for owned banks, anchors each bank under the per-CPU device, discovers blocks recursively and fully rolls back on any bank failure before publishing the array and optionally installing the threshold vector. Discovery ignores out-of-range positions, unreadable registers and entries lacking usable counting including locked ones. Teardown nulls the per-CPU pointer before releasing blocks, banks and the array, with object release freeing its container. Naming prefers legacy fourth-bank specialisation, then legacy positional labels, then memory-controller block labels, numbered block fallback, numbered bank fallback and singleton versus instanced family labels.
Firmware error interchange packs a common record header plus section descriptor plus native machine-check payload with no padding, so offsets remain stable for firmware consumers.

Four firmware-backed operations persist a machine-check as a fatal single-section record with previous-error marking, iterate stored records skipping concurrently cleared entries until an invalid terminator, report the stored count and clear by identifier.
A global mutex object exists to coordinate machine-check sysfs access.

Machine-check topology keeps a per-CPU bank count plus a per-CPU array of bank descriptors sized by the architectural maximum. User visibility uses a fixed array pairing attribute metadata and short names with bank numbers. Vendor flags and global configuration are marked mostly read, with two timeout and logging controls defaulting to negative one. Recent hardware errors are tracked per CPU.

Tracing scaffolding is enabled at build time. Poll coverage defaults to all banks enabled. A global mask records banks with corrected-error reporting disabled. Deferred handling uses both process and interrupt contexts plus a per-CPU injection slot for testing.
Decoder registration accepts only priorities within the defined lowest to highest window and otherwise ignores the request, with symmetric unregister for chain membership.

Energy-bias control exposes a single power-group attribute. Online brings restore before optional sysfs merge, while offline does optional unmerge before save, with merge activity suppressed while tasks are frozen. Initialisation requires the energy-bias feature, optionally overrides the normal hint on matched models and registers hotplug plus suspend-resume handling, unwinding hotplug on failure.

A shared attribute vector slot is rewritten according to each block capability, so concurrent population may race. Generated names reuse one global scratch buffer, so callers must consume immediately. Unexpected fourth-bank addresses trigger a kernel warning path. Early deferred interrupts before vector installation hit a reporting stub rather than polling.

Limit programming and count display fail cleanly when the owning CPU is offline or unreachable. Block discovery recurses across linked addresses and must terminate on a null link. Removal publishes null before freeing to avoid interrupt use-after-free. Bank creation failures discard all previously built banks to avoid partial sysfs.
